analysis: The two supplied units are base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 20278-21629). They contain public synthetic cache-parity vectors: repeated filler text, token IDs, prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries and chain hashes. These base excerpts lie outside the changed base ranges listed in file_changes; the nearest changed base lines are 3024-4824, 43813, 44591, 44692, 45533, 52418, 53196, 53297 and 54138. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could see only the first hunk. That hunk adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to a fixture, changes prompt_token_count from 803 to 767, drops the 768-token block boundary and updates the chain hashes. This is a test-vector change with no runtime code, no keys or secrets, no authorization, attestation, encryption or billing logic. It touches no TB-011, TB-002 or A-001 control. The content is explicitly public synthetic data, so I identified no confidentiality exposure. The one residual security-relevant question is integration: these vectors back the T-041 prefix-cache design (HMAC-keyed block chain hashes), and the corresponding Swift/Go prompt-contract code must produce matching hashes for the new enable_thinking context. A mismatch would at worst break cache parity or availability, not trust. I did not see the changed source files or the rest of the patch, so I cannot confirm that. I report no finding.
